Transfers & Breakout Stars

Did Changing Colleges Actually Boost Hitting Between 2021 and 2022?

With the rise of the NCAA transfer portal, it is easy to assume that switching colleges automatically unlocks bigger numbers at the plate. Across the 1,135 players who recorded full Division I seasons in both 2021 and 2022, 72 switched Division I programs while 1,063 stayed at the same college.

The data tells a surprising two-part story:

  1. Transfers were already above-average hitters before leaving. Players who changed schools averaged a .847 OPS in 2021—well ahead of the .801 OPS posted by players who stayed put.
  2. Changing jerseys wasn’t an automatic boost—but the right fit created superstars. On average, transfers gained just +0.003 OPS in 2022 (compared to +0.016 OPS for returning players), because many moved up into tougher pitching conferences. Yet when a transfer found the right lineup, the leap was dramatic: KB Sides transferred from Alabama to Arkansas and jumped from 0 home runs (.811 OPS) to 13 home runs (1.212 OPS), while Alyssa Brito moved from Oregon to Oklahoma and climbed from .936 to 1.190 OPS (14 HRs).
